scraped.title: Zoomers want to be shocked
scraped.author: Sam Jennings
scraped.h1: Zoomers want to be shocked “The Devils’ challenges our sexless digital anomie”
scraped.body_text:
“Russell is a maximalist with an intensely morbid streak.” (The Devils/YouTube)

“Russell is a maximalist with an intensely morbid streak.” (The Devils/YouTube)

Think quick: when was the last time you remember a film causing a serious controversy? Not just a bit of handwringing from critics, or swarms of angry commentators online — but actual, real-world protest, even censorship? The closest thing might be Todd Phillips’s Joker, back in 2019, which initiated a minor media blitz warning of possible shootings and incel-adjacent terrorist activity. Though of course nothing remotely bad ever happened: the film went on to be the highest-grossing R-rated movie ever, and even won two Oscars.

We live in a world where self-righteous outrage and vengeful online fandoms are endless and ubiquitous — given the ease with which people (regardless of political persuasion) take to the internet to decry some book or film or artist as immoral and worthy of cancellation, one could be forgiven for thinking that modern audiences are constantly being confronted with truly shocking, and offensive art. Why, then, does it seem like cinema has in fact never been more risk-averse, tepid, and oppressively homogeneous?

Take a film like The Drama , which did surprisingly well for its studio, A24, back in May. A film like that may benefit, as The Drama did, from early buzz around a few supposedly controversial plot points, in this case a lengthy scene in which Zendaya’s character confesses to planning, but never executing, a school shooting as a young bullied kid. One or two negative reviews popped up, citing its being vaguely “problematic,” whether because the film didn’t highlight the racial implications enough, or because the critic deemed it insensitive to find comedy in something like a school shooting. But then the film came and the “controversy” was hardly that: instead it’s a decent satire on the Puritanical anxieties of upper-middle class Millennials in big coastal American cities. Nobody batted an eye, the film did well, then the film was gone. Robert Pattinson and Zendaya starred in all the other giant blockbusters of 2026, and no one was truly offended.

The question remains: what would audiences do, if presented with something actually shocking? Something upsettingly sexual, violent, and blithely offensive towards every institution within spitting distance? Well, Ken Russell’s infamous 1971 film The Devils has returned to the big screen to answer that very question, and the answer appears to be: people like it. A lot. Due to popular demand, the film has already extended past its initial week-long run in the US, where it has already made more than $4 million, truly remarkable for a repertory release. Last week it opened in the UK. Critical reviews have been rapturous, almost in direct proportion to how disappointed reviewers were 55 years ago. What seemed over-the-top, heavy-handed, and cynical to the critics in 1971 now seems rather loony, courageous, and thoroughly committed to its own extremity.

So how is it that a film made more than half a century ago ago — one that was censored, truncated, and dismissed by critics for decades — has become the most exciting “new” film of 2026? One immediate answer is that the extraordinary 4K restoration of Russell’s official director’s cut, first assembled in 2004 but never shown in cinemas, gives today’s audiences the very things we’re often told they don’t want: graphic nudity, semi-pornographic sex acts (many involving religious icons; one involving a burnt human femur), surrealism, absurdism, camp, Expressionism, vulgarity — not to mention a complex but ultimately heroic protagonist defined by his unapologetic virility, spiritual seriousness, hypocrisy, and pride. The film is an orgiastic, sadistic, Dionysian picture of the French Wars of Religion as a kind of depraved and cynical theater: one which in Russell’s hands overflows with all the destructive energy, unashamed Romanticism, and individualism of the countercultural Sixties.

Based on a play by John Whiting and a novel by Aldous Huxley, the film was financed by Warner Brothers in 1971. The studio threw a serious amount of money behind it, enabling Russell and his set designer, a young Derek Jarman, to build a series of mammoth sets at Pinewood Studios, outside of London, filling it with hundreds of extras and filming for months in difficult conditions. As a work of pure cinematic technique, the film is a masterpiece. Russell is a maximalist with an intensely morbid streak and a love for the grotesque: he uses the setting of the play and the novel as a canvas on which to paint every bit of religious hypocrisy and sexual decadence imaginable. Yet underneath the burnings, tortures, church-floor orgies, convent exorcisms, and cackling audiences of evil French decadents, there’s an almost naive, sentimental insistence on the power of love and self-belief. Russell is always daring you to reconcile these extremes, always baiting his audience not to take him seriously. But he is, in his rascal way, very serious about certain things. Shortly after the film’s release, he was asked in an interview what he thought audiences should look for in his work, and replied, without a hint of irony, “Two contrasts: the force of nature and truth and beauty, against the corruption of a decadent society. That’s what I think all my films are about.” What could be more Romantic?

Thus the real heart of the film is its main character’s progress toward sincere martyrdom: Father Urbain Grandier (Oliver Reed) begins the film as the de facto leader of the walled French commune of Loudun, a man who loves the pomp and power afforded him by his priesthood, and considers himself above the problems of the people. At the same time, he prays earnestly for the dying, and genuinely tries to protect the city from Cardinal Richelieu’s ministers, who want to tear down the city’s fortifications to prevent the possible sheltering of Huguenots. Grandier’s downfall begins with the obsession of Sister Jeanne (Vanessa Redgrave), an insane hunchbacked nun shut away in the town’s Ursuline convent. Jeanne is consumed with erotic dreams of Grandier as Christ; when she learns Grandier has fallen in love and married in secret, she accuses him of possessing her through Satan-worship. This initiates a full-on exorcism and a macabre show-trial, which turns into a full-on orgy in the Loudun cathedral, ending in the Grandier’s burning at the stake. The way Russell orchestrates it, you get a morbid sense that this is what both religious and political power have always used — these moments of ritualized madness, rape, and abandon — to manipulate a population which has to be cowed and sexually repressed the rest of the time.

In this sense, The Devils bears an extraordinarily complicated relation to the chaotic decade that preceded it, a period which gave birth to cheap exploitation cinema and a new wave of producers willing to risk money on spectacles designed to draw audiences to violent and sexually explicit content — an era which effectively ended with the financial disasters of Francis Ford Coppola’s Apocalypse Now (1979) and Michael Cimino’s Heaven’s Gate (1980). But nowhere did this risk-taking impulse join with the countercultural zeitgeist like it did in Ken Russell’s films. Russell was the ultimate filmmaker of the Free Love generation — something that was already apparent with his brilliant 1969 adaptation of D. H. Lawrence’s Women in Love . With his great run of Seventies films — including Lisztomania, The Music Lovers, Mahler, and his psychedelic adaptation of The Who’s rock opera Tommy — Russell created one of the most outré and avant-garde filmographies in the history of mainstream cinema. His favorite subjects were always tortured artists, and his style was unapologetically flamboyant, theatrical, and aggressive. But it was with The Devils that he pushed his concerns into darker, riskier territory: the film’s most disturbing set-pieces are shocking not just because of the debauchery they show, but because those acts are mixed with so much bleak humor, and finally somewhat redeemed by the earnest martyrdom of Father Grandier, who becomes the Christ-like scapegoat for an entire society’s perversion and evil.

This is why it’s so interesting that contemporary audiences are taking to the film. Two decades of bitter online fandoms, culture warriors, and internet commentators have led to a moviegoing public that generally treats its films as objects in an ideological contest. The Zoomer and Alpha discomfort with sex and nudity in film is well-known. And everyone is familiar with the Millennial tendency — amongst fervent conservatives and progressives alike — to call for the cancellation of any artists or media they perceive to be opposed to their own political programmes. We live in a climate that is generally inhospitable to artists, whether due to the domination of corporate entertainment, or the widespread sentiment that the goal of art is to provide its audience with a moral directive, and never to risk offending the wrong people.

By Barry lyndon

I suspect that what The Devils is offering its audience is exactly the kind of dangerous, unstable, kinetic wildness that’s missing from the current film landscape — as well as a heady charge of moral complexity and Romantic seriousness. The overwhelming tenor of contemporary film is one of intense claustrophobia, malaise, and overdetermination — just look at those two surprise Gen Z successes this year, Obsession and Backrooms . We’re often told that young audiences want original films, and high ticket sales this year — the highest since before the Covid pandemic — have apparently been driven by younger audiences . Certainly the remarkable success of those films attests to this. Still, consider their actual tone and structure: both films are airless nightmares about the total loss of self, with a film grammar as locked-down and exhaustively composed as any “elevated horror film” made within the past 15 years. There’s no room within their compact frames for any experiment — never any genuine sense of abandon, no real risk, nothing truly shocking . Nothing about contemporary cinema actively goes against the normal mainstream culture, not even the original films young audiences want.

In total contrast to the majority of contemporary films, the real excitement of Russell’s The Devils is just how wildly loose, dangerous — and, yes, free — it feels. The film is an argument for the right to be violent, sexual, voyeuristic, obscene, and offensive to anyone and everything. True, it portrays dozens of the kinds of acts young people today tend to get very squeamish and upset over, but it does so in the service of an intense, passionate plea for freedom itself: for the freedom to love, for total artistic freedom, for freedom from religion and political oppression and sexual repression. It remains remarkably countercultural — and this is exactly what contemporary audiences are gravitating toward. They sense that cinema is at a kind of frigid deadlock, just as our broader culture seems to be heading toward a sexless and Puritanical digital anomie that hates the human body, and denigrates the realities of human love.

The Devils is the most exciting film of 2026 because it is the most countercultural film of 2026. What precisely “countercultural” means in 2026 is, of course, almost impossible to envision. We’re drowning in a shallow pool of endless content, most of which might as well have been made by machines. We have no real observable subcultures; we lack any sense of “scenes” or “movements”; most cities now are too expensive for these things to organically emerge, so successful creatives tend to be so because they were either born into wealth, or lucked out after years of hopeless struggle. But The Devils is a reminder of what it once looked like to make something genuinely offensive and risky — and, astoundingly, it feels wilder and more dangerous than anything any filmmaker has made in this century. Everything about it is a challenge to our exhausted, cynical, post-Romantic assumptions. And everyone who goes to see it knows this, deep down. Let’s hope the revival lasts a long time. The people clearly need it.

Sam Jennings is an American writer and musician living in London. More of his writing can be found at his Substack, Vita Contemplativa .

scraped.title: 'They're Coming For The Rest Of Us': Jon Stewart Nods Along As Maddow Comes Unglued Over Trump 'Mega-Prisons'
scraped.description: ZeroHedge - On a long enough timeline, the survival rate for everyone drops to zero
scraped.author: Tyler Durden
scraped.h1: 'They're Coming For The Rest Of Us': Jon Stewart Nods Along As Maddow Comes Unglued Over Trump 'Mega-Prisons'
scraped.body_text:
MS NOW host Rachel Maddow told Jon Stewart on Monday's The Daily Show that if President Trump gets the giant warehouse prisons his administration has sought for immigrants, they won't stay immigrant-only for long.

"With a president like this, if you give him seven to ten prisons around the country that hold 10,000 people each, where he can hold people without trial, without access to lawyers indefinitely, you think he's only going to leave immigrants in there?" Maddow asked. "I just don't. I think that what they first do to immigrants, they want to do to the rest of us."

On "Comedy Central," Rachel Maddow very seriously says Trump wants to put his opponents in mega-prisons next to the illegal aliens slated for deportation. pic.twitter.com/CPVuD8C8Jb

— Tim Graham (@TimJGraham) November 13, 2026

The exchange started with the Department of Homeland Security's plan to turn a warehouse in Social Circle, Georgia, into a detention center for up to 10,000 people, which DHS dropped in June after the city fought it. Stewart said many of the people being held were in for what are usually treated as civil matters. "These are not the worst of the worst. These are people who overstayed a student visa or are here on a green card but got a parking ticket."

Maddow added people who came in under temporary protected status, saying the administration "basically illegalized people who had never done anything illegal in their life." Then she told Stewart that treating detention as an immigration issue misses the point: "We think about it as a special class of behavior by the government that's just for immigrants. And we think, therefore, oh, you either care about immigrants or you don't. No, I'm sorry."

White House spokesman Davis Ingle told Fox News that "Jon Stewart is a talentless hack who clearly suffers from a severe and debilitating disease known as Trump Derangement Syndrome that has rotted his peanut-sized brain and ruined his life." Former RNC spokesperson Elizabeth Pipko said the pair were conflating immigrants with illegal immigrants, adding that legal immigrants "are not targets for deportation or arrest by immigration officers. Rachel Maddow and Jon Stewart both know that."

Maddow was on the show to promote her new book on the Justice Department, Department of Fate , six days after Democrats' midterm sweep . Asked what Democratic leaders in the House and Senate should do with their new power, Maddow said they should act "not only to investigate what's been going on with ICE, but to defund what ICE has been doing," and impeach "not only Pete Hegseth, but Todd Blanche."

"I think that's important not just to shame those guys, but in some cases it's essentially to stop a crime wave in progress," she said.

Rachel @maddow explains what she'd like to see from Democrats: investigate ICE, impeach Pete Hegseth and Todd Blanche, make healthcare more affordable for all, and more pic.twitter.com/otqflN1vGR

— The Daily Show (@TheDailyShow) November 10, 2026

Republicans in the outgoing House blocked Rep. Thomas Massie's impeachment articles against Hegseth this week, with 11 Democrats missing the vote , which leaves the effort for the new Congress in January. Attorney General Blanche has refused to rule out prosecuting Democratic lawmakers who plan to investigate Trump officials , after the President ordered the Justice Department to look into what he called a "criminal act."

Maddow also called for health insurance for every child in America through a bill from Sen. Andy Kim, and a ban on political donations from federal contractors. When Stewart asked, "No stock trading?" she said a ban on members of Congress trading stocks would go "on the floor first day."

"I think they can use the power of the purse to stop the Iran war," Maddow said.

scraped.description: ZeroHedge - On a long enough timeline, the survival rate for everyone drops to zero
scraped.author: Tyler Durden
scraped.h1: 'You're A F***ing Liar!": The DSA Is Out For Blood, Targets Jeffries, Schumer, & Others
scraped.body_text:
A protester heckled House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) in Denver on Friday , as he campaigns to become speaker of the House when the new Democratic majority takes over in January.

The man interrupted Jeffries while he spoke onstage at the What's Next conference, where Democratic leaders, strategists, and newly elected lawmakers gathered to plan how to use the new majorities and how to position the party for 2028.

The protester shouted, "You are a f****** liar!" at Jeffries. He kept yelling for more than a minute while the crowd booed , and the shouting continued until his removal from the building.

🚨 HOLY CRAP! Hakeem Jeffries is getting EATEN ALIVE by protestors right in the middle of his remarks "You are a f*cking LIAR!" "You're a f*cking TRAITOR!" For nearly 2 MINUTES STRAIGHT they were getting hauled out as they went berserk The clown car is DESTROYING ITSELF 🤣 pic.twitter.com/TXmXNk3lbU

— Eric Daugherty (@EricLDaugh) November 13, 2026

When the moderator noted that Jeffries had stayed calm during the interruption, Jeffries said, "Remember, ya'll, I grew up in Brooklyn." The discussion resumed once the protester was gone.

This is hardly the first sign of tension between Jeffries and the DSA-wing of the party. At a June victory event for Rep.-elect Valdez (D-NY) after New York's Democratic primaries, Democratic Socialists of America activists celebrated their candidates' wins by chanting "You're next!" as a picture of Jeffries appeared on a screen . The chant targeted the highest-ranking Democrat in the House. Jeffries did not face a primary challenger in 2026. Friction between the party establishment and the DSA has continued since Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress on November 3.

Jeffries succeeded Nancy Pelosi (D-CA) as House Democratic leader in January 2023 and no Democrat has formally challenged Jeffries for speaker. Parts of the party's progressive wing object to his support for Israel and his ties to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), and some incoming lawmakers have not endorsed him.

House Democrats have their internal leadership elections on Nov 18th and Jeffries is by a long way the favorite to win. The Speaker sets the agenda for the House, decides which bills reach the floor, and is a key player in negotiations with the Senate and the White House. Progressives have criticized the party's response to President Donald Trump, and a petition calling for new Democratic leadership has drawn more than 1.1 million signatures . No lawmaker has come forward to challenge him.

The Senate leadership race already has a contender.

Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) announced Thursday that he will challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY) for majority leader , with backing from Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) and Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-MI). Schumer said he has the votes to keep the job.

DSA and its allies have begun lining up 2028 primary challenges against sitting Democrats, according to Newsweek . The group grew its House caucus from two members to eight in the midterms and helped elect El-Sayed to the Senate.

Sen. John Fetterman (D-PA) already has a declared challenger, Ahmed Moor, a 42-year-old Palestinian American writer and dues-paying member of Philadelphia DSA. Moor is campaigning on ending the war in Iran and "free healthcare, free childcare, and affordable housing." Fetterman has not said whether he will seek a second term.

A July Quinnipiac poll found 19% of Pennsylvania Democrats approved of Fetterman's job performance, while 69% disapproved. The Pennsylvania Working Families Party pledged in November 2025 to back a challenger. Allies of Rep. Summer Lee (D-PA), a democratic socialist, want her to enter the race. Lee posted, "2028 can't come fast enough for PA." Gov. Josh Shapiro (D-PA) said he expects "a robust primary challenge" if Fetterman runs.

For Schumer, the central question is whether Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) runs against him. She has said she would make "any of those considerations after the midterms." Schumer, 75, has not said whether he will seek a sixth term. A 2025 Data for Progress survey of likely New York Democratic primary voters showed Ocasio-Cortez leading Schumer 55% to 36%. Polymarket gives her 56% odds of running for president and 31.8% odds of running for Senate.

If Ocasio-Cortez pursues the presidency instead, New York City Council Member Chi Ossé, a DSA member, says he would run against Schumer as the socialist alternative .

Ossé dropped an exploratory challenge to Jeffries in 2025 after Zohran Mamdani urged NYC-DSA not to endorse, and the chapter's electoral working group voted 52% to 46% against backing him. NYC-DSA co-chair Grace Mausser has not ruled out a challenge to Jeffries in 2028 or 2030. "Hakeem Jeffries only cares about keeping the corporate donations rolling in ," Mausser said.

Streamer Hasan Piker named Rep. Hillary Scholten (D-MI) a top 2028 primary target . Scholten had refused to endorse El-Sayed and called Piker "a hack who thrives on hate, shock and awe because he lacks substance." Her Grand Rapids district offers more competitive ground than DSA's deep-blue strongholds in New York City.

Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY) defeated anti-AIPAC challenger Michael Blake 71.95% to 21.81% in June. NYC-DSA co-chair Gustavo Gordillo said "Ritchie Torres needs to break ties with AIPAC " to avoid a DSA-backed challenge. Torres has called DSA "despicable, detestable, disgraceful, and disgraced."

In 2025, CNN listed Rep. Yvette Clarke (D-NY) alongside Jeffries, Torres, Rep. Jerry Nadler (D-NY), and Rep. Dan Goldman (D-NY) as members that Mamdani allies wanted to unseat. Nadler has since retired, and Goldman lost his race.

NYC-DSA has not publicly named new House targets since the midterms. The chapter says its membership has doubled to more than 12,000.

scraped.title: As Dems Take Congress, Alito Warns They Can "Turn Off The Lights" At Supreme Court
scraped.description: ZeroHedge - On a long enough timeline, the survival rate for everyone drops to zero
scraped.author: Tyler Durden
scraped.h1: As Dems Take Congress, Alito Warns They Can "Turn Off The Lights" At Supreme Court
scraped.body_text:
Authored by Jack Phillips via The Epoch Times ,

Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito said Thursday that he is concerned Congress could make decisions that affect the high court's funding.

"Congress can turn off the lights at the Supreme Court and stop everything from happening if they want to defund their activities. And there are many, many, many other things that they can do, or at least try to do," Alito said at a Federalist Society event on Thursday.

"So, it is important to preserve the independence of the judiciary," he remarked, adding that " if that is eliminated, then the Constitution as adopted in 1789 will no longer be the same. "

Alito said at the event that the judiciary is the least powerful branch of the government, compared with Congress and the executive. But he still warned that judges can wield too much power and added that some lower-court judges have issued rulings blocking presidents' orders that he believes were unjustified.

"If you think about a hand grenade, a 500-pound bomb and a nuclear weapon," he said, "the hand grenade is the least dangerous. But that is not to say that it is not dangerous."

Judges can be "dedicated" and "skillful," but Alito warned, "they're not perfect, and they make mistakes."

"And in some instances, I think they have gone far astray in abuse of their powers."

Over the summer, Justices Elena Kagan and Amy Coney Barrett testified before Congress to seek more security funding for the Supreme Court amid rising threats against the institution , including after a 2022 leak of an opinion that overturned Roe v. Wade, penned by Alito.

Following the 2022 leak, a suspect, Nicholas Roske, was arrested for the attempted assassination of Justice Brett Kavanaugh outside his home. Roske was later convicted and sentenced to eight years in prison.

"Maybe I lack imagination, but I didn't expect that performing this service was going to put me in the position of explaining to my children what a bulletproof vest was and why I had to wear one," Barrett told a House committee in mid-July.

The justice added that security-related threats have also forced her children to "think about and see things that children should not have to see or think about."

Alito's comments Thursday came after Democrats made significant gains during the midterm elections earlier this month and regained control over both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Some Democratic lawmakers have proposed changes to the Supreme Court, including term limits on justices, who are appointed by a president to serve for life unless they resign or are impeached and removed.

In July, a group of Democratic senators said they want 18-year term limits and "regularized appointments" for justices , with Sen. Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) arguing in a statement that the institution has seen "unacceptable levels of politicization."

Beyond term limits, some Democratic members have said they want to expand the court past the nine-member limit. Rep. Jim Clyburn (D-S.C.) said in an NBC interview on Aug. 30 he thought the court should expand to 13 members.

Earlier this year, the House rejected an effort to cap the Supreme Court at nine justices. A resolution introduced by Rep. Andy Biggs (R-Ariz.) would have proposed a constitutional amendment.

The mass build-up of data centers across the United States has sparked a massive backlash for mostly understandable reasons. But one anti-data center activist went too far, and a resurfaced video perfectly explains why.

As NPR reported last week, a Maryland woman named Taylor Frazier McCollum successfully helped block a $5 billion data center campus that was supposed to be built on nearly 90 acres of empty land in Landover, Md.

This land used to be Landover Mall.

In 2024, the developer that built the mall won approval from county planners for the data center.

McCollum lived less than a mile away from the proposed project and quickly sprang into action.

“I was like, ‘Oh, hell no,'” she told NPR. “Why would you want to bring water-polluting, diesel-generating data centers right down the street from where people live, work, play? It just didn’t make sense to me.”

McCollum then created a petition in June 2025 that initially failed to take off until the Marxist Party for Socialism and Liberation (PSL), which is linked to Beijing-based tech mogul and left-wing donor Neville Roy Singham, shared a video of her explaining the petition and accusing the data center developers of “environmental racism.”

With the PSL’s help, the petition garnered 25,000 signatures.

In September 2025, Prince George’s County executive Aisha Braveboy issued a ‘temporary’ moratorium on data center permits, halting the Landover project. This moratorium has been extended several times and is set to expire at the end of this year.

McCollum now wants the area filled with a trampoline park, which would generate far less revenue than the data center would.

Now, a video has emerged via The Daily Wire that explains the worldview of communists like McCollum and the fantasy world they live in.

In the video, McCollum claims that money is just a “made-up concept.” That is news to the billions of people around the world who use some form of currency every day to conduct business and make a living.

“Money, you know, is a made-up concept,” she says in the video. “We buy into it every day and choose to say that this has value, and that doesn’t have value.”

Maryland activist who blocked a $5 billion data center from coming to her cash-strapped county says “money is a made-up concept.” https://t.co/PGFHwqKWYp

scraped.body_text:
Guest post by Terry Newsome

A long-running Rose City ANTIFA Facebook Page and many others remain active on the platform even after being designated as a domestic terrorist organization .

Facebook continues to show a clear double standard. It allows ANTIFA-linked pages and users to remain active—even after the White House’s September 22, 2025 Executive Order that designates ANTIFA a “domestic terrorist organization” and directs agencies to investigate, disrupt, and dismantle illegal operations by ANTIFA or anyone claiming to act on its behalf. Facebook ignores the designation while restricting conservatives who document confrontations, acts of violence, and targeted harassment.

ANTIFA cells weaponized Facebook to organize, track ICE, coordinate global activities, and target their adversaries. Conservative pro-ICE supporters have faced coordinated efforts in which ANTIFA-linked users stalked their accounts, posted threats and derogatory comments, and launched mass-reporting campaigns.

Facebook defines mass reporting as an adversarial tactic —coordinated networks working to get content “incorrectly taken down”—and its Inauthentic Behavior rules explicitly prohibit misusing the reporting system to harass, intimidate, or silence people. Yet when Antifa-linked users have flooded videos and posts that document confrontations, Facebook has repeatedly issued penalizing strikes and account restrictions against the people posting that material.

One clear example is Facebook’s long-running tolerance of Rose City ANTIFA, one of the country’s oldest and most active cells. This group has a documented history of violence and doxxing—including members tied to the June 2019 beating of journalist Andy Ngo in Portland, for which some individuals were later ordered to pay damages in civil court—and has targeted law enforcement .

In August 2026, the State Department and Treasury designated the Italy-based Autistici/Inventati network as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist for supplying encrypted tools, hosting, and other digital infrastructure used by Rose City ANTIFA and other Antifa-linked cells. DHS and the State Department have specifically flagged the group (and closely associated sites such as Rose City Counter-Info) for doxxing ICE officers and issuing threats against them.

Despite these actions and the group’s record, Facebook has allowed Rose City ANTIFA to maintain an active page. Facebook’s stated policy of removing groups that pose significant public-safety risks has not resulted in the page’s removal—even after multiple reports and public criticism—while the platform continues to restrict conservatives who document ANTIFA confrontations and has not applied equivalent scrutiny to the harassment and mass-reporting campaigns directed against them.

One clear case involves videos from the Chicago ICE Center. A lone 71-year-old man holding a “I Support Law Enforcement” sign was surrounded by protesters and ANTIFA members, including Fran Ocequeda and Harrison Quinn Wahl, who verbally assaulted the elderly man. Illinois conservative activist Terry Newsome was driving past, stopped to help, and immediately became the target. Ocequeda got in his face and threatened to kill him while he was surrounded; Newsome responded aggressively after the threat. Facebook removed Newsome’s video of the confrontation and issued a violation strike. His account then faced limits: no monetization, no recommendations to other users, restricted features, and content not recommended to non-followers. The response ignored the video evidence of who initiated the confrontation with the elderly man and the threats that followed.

Fran Ocequeda and others surround Newsome at the Chicago ICE Center after he stops to help a 71-year-old veteran after being assaulted. Facebook gave Newsome a violation for posting the confrontation. The Facebook moderator calls ANTIFA “private citizen protesters.” Judge for yourself. WARNING: ADULT LANGUAGE

Watch here.

The Gateway Pundit obtained an internal communication from Facebook’s moderation team addressing a request to review the targeted harassment of Terry Newsome’s account and reconsider the strikes he received through coordinated mass reporting by ANTIFA. In the response, the moderator said the account had not been disabled but faced limits of no monetization, no recommendations to other users, and some restricted features stemming from a series of strikes for content that broke Community Standards. The reviewer claimed to have looked at every active strike, with extra care on a specific video, and concluded that most strikes were for “repeated content attacking or insulting private individuals, including protesters.” The moderator said these were applied correctly and in line with policies, found no sign that political views played any part, and noted that a second review by the policy team confirmed the decision. Remaining strikes would stay in place until they expire.

Facebook moderator’s description does not match the facts. The claim that Newsome’s strikes were justified for attacking ordinary “private individuals, including protesters” is false .

The people Newsome interacted with—whether through posts documenting confrontations or responses to those harassing and stalking him on his own page—were ANTIFA members or far-left radicals who were the aggressors. Video shows them surrounding and harassing an elderly man, issuing threats, and then using mass community reports to trigger enforcement against the person who recorded it.

If the moderation team had actually looked at the context, the identities of those involved, or the pattern of coordinated reporting instead of accepting surface-level claims, the strikes for exposing ANTIFA activity would not have been upheld. Instead, Facebook protected the aggressors while penalizing Newsome’s visibility, growth, monetization, and account health for pushing back. The moderator’s assertion that political views played no role and that the strikes were correctly applied ignores the evidence and reflects a clear double standard.

Facebook’s moderators repeatedly described the people in Newsome’s videos and interactions as ordinary “private individuals, including protesters.” The following clips show additional confrontations with the same category of individuals at ICE-related events—none of which resulted in strikes against Newsome, but which illustrate the people Facebook has characterized that way.

March 8, 2026, at the Broadview ICE facility (the same location where Emily Cahill was assaulted). Raven Geary, an ANTIFA-associated activist, spits in Newsome’s face. Broadview police charged her with assault.

On January 17, 2026, Emily Cahill—a local conservative ICE supporter and leader of Protest the Protesters, was brutally assaulted at the Chicago/Broadview ICE center while simply holding a “We Love ICE” sign. Anti-ICE organizer Chela Garcia snuck up behind her, ripped her hair, and punched her repeatedly. When Cahill tried to fight back, a pack of male Antifa members grabbed and held her so Garcia could continue her assault.

Watch here.

Emily Cahill’s Facebook post of the Assault by Chela Garcia and ANTIFA at the Broadview ICE Center

Trending: President Trump MUST Declare a National Emergency and Nullify 2026 Midterm Elections or the Country We Know and Love Will Be Lost Forever!

The January 17, 2026 Broadview rally was organized by Indivisible collaborator Carlos Álvarez-Aranyos, founder of American Opposition and a key strategist behind anti-Trump and “No Kings” protests. Álvarez-Aranyos previously worked for Protect Democracy, a group funded by George Soros’s Open Society Foundations.

Newsome reposted Cahill’s original January 17 th Facebook post of the assault—Cahills identical post is still up on her page while Facebook removed Newsome’s for a violation. He appealed. Human moderators reviewed the clear video of ANTIFA and Garcia assaulting Cahill but still upheld the strike. Facebook once again protected ANTIFA attackers while punishing the conservative who documented their violence. Facebook admits coordinated mass reporting as a problem, yet it still refuses to explain why its human moderators keep showing clear bias against conservative accounts.

Emily Cahill’s post of the January 17 th assault. Cahill’s post remains up while Newsome’s was removed due to mass fake reporting by ANTIFA.

Watch here.

Other strikes followed the same pattern. They covered replies to users who were already targeting and commenting on Newsome’s account, along with posts that exposed ANTIFA activity. Facebook claimed these posts violated its policies on bullying, harassment, hateful conduct, or violence and incitement. The appeal response failed to address the prior stalking, the coordinated mass reporting, or the fact that the people initiating contact were the aggressors.

Recently, another conservative, Tom Kaz—known on Facebook as the Crazy Conservative Roofer—was at the same Broadview ICE Center where Terry Newsome and Emily Cahill were previously assaulted. While reciting the Pledge of Allegiance, he was verbally harassed by ANTIFA members who yelled “F*** You” at him through a bullhorn. He posted the video of the confrontation on Facebook; it was removed for “hateful conduct.” Once again, the conservative who documented the confrontation was punished.

It also took down another video showing Christian conservatives protesting. Facebook justified the removals under its community standards, labeling the content as potentially containing “symbols, glorification or support of people and organizations we define as dangerous.”

The irony is hard to miss. A cross, a Bible, and Americans reciting the Pledge of Allegiance were treated as dangerous, while Facebook continues to allow active pages and organizing by ANTIFA. The screenshot on the far right shows Muse, Facebook’s AI, responding to the conservative’s questions about why his account was suddenly targeted after he counter-protested at the Chicago/Broadview ICE Center. The AI’s answer was not surprising: it indicated the account had become the target of mass reporting.

This enforcement contrasts with Facebook’s aggressive removal of Proud Boys content and bans on the group. While ANTIFA—described in the September 22, 2025 Executive Order as a militarist, anarchist enterprise that uses illegal means including organized riots, assaults on ICE and law enforcement, and doxing to suppress lawful political activity—maintains a presence and weaponizes reporting tools, Proud Boys material is routinely removed.

The result is a platform that allows a group designated a domestic terrorist organization by Executive Order to organize, harass, and silence conservatives through mass reporting, while penalizing the people who record the confrontations or push back. Facebook’s claim that political views played no role does not hold up against the pattern of removals, the content of the videos, the internal moderation response that treated ANTIFA aggressors as ordinary “private individuals and protesters,” or the platform’s double standard toward other groups. Those who coordinate false or bad-faith mass reports to trigger enforcement should face consequences under Facebook’s own rules against misusing the reporting system. Conservatives documenting ANTIFA activity should not be the ones restricted while the original aggressors continue operating freely on the platform.

Americans should not cede their sovereignty because you all have suicidal empathy.”

items.summary: The transportation secretary says overloaded routers forced the FAA to halt flights and urges Congress to fund a new air traffic control system. Source

scraped.title: Duffy Blames Outdated System After Nationwide Flight Ground Stop › American Greatness
scraped.description: The transportation secretary says overloaded routers forced the FAA to halt flights and urges Congress to fund a new air traffic control system.
scraped.h1: Duffy Blames Outdated System After Nationwide Flight Ground Stop
scraped.body_text:
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Friday that aging equipment was to blame for a nationwide ground stop that halted flights across the country, Breitbart News reported.

Hours after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights in the United States, Duffy told reporters at the White House that the system’s routers became overwhelmed. The FAA alert had read, “BY ORDER OF THE FEDERAL AVIATION COMMAND CENTER ALL AIRPORTS ARE GROUND STOPPED.” Flights later resumed.

“So, what happened? I’ve heard a lot of the rumors, like Markwayne has,” Duffy said, referring to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, who appeared with him. “But, what we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system.”

Duffy explained that the system still relies on analog telecommunications. “Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data, and they went down,” he said. He then clarified that the routers “started to give us inconsistency in the data,” adding, “and because of that we shut the system down.”

Mullin had said earlier that there was “no indication” the outage was the result of a “nefarious attack.”

Duffy said the problem is not new. He pointed to outages at Newark a year and a half ago and called the failures a continual problem. Controllers, he said, are working in facilities with “leaky roofs” and “air conditioning that doesn’t work.”

“I think every single one of your networks have covered the President and myself talking about this for the last two years,” Duffy said. He said that he and President Trump asked Congress for $30 billion to build a new system, and that he would like to see $50 billion.

“Let’s not do a patchwork, a fix to a system that’s critical for every single family,” Duffy said. “It’s not red. It’s not blue. It’s not Democrat. It’s not Republican. It’s American. Give us the money to fix it.”

The ground stop is the latest sign that decades of neglect have left America’s air traffic control system dangerously outdated. Washington talked about modernization for years.

items.title: Trump Administration Tells Federal Agencies to Operate in English
items.summary: New Justice Department guidance directs agencies to drop most foreign-language materials that are not required by law. Source

scraped.title: Trump Administration Tells Federal Agencies to Operate in English › American Greatness
scraped.description: New Justice Department guidance directs agencies to drop most foreign-language materials that are not required by law.
scraped.h1: Trump Administration Tells Federal Agencies to Operate in English
scraped.body_text:
The Trump administration is directing federal agencies to conduct their business in English, the New York Post reported on the sweeping new directive.

The Justice Department guidance, published in the Federal Register this week, carries out President Trump’s March 2025 executive order designating English as the official language of the federal government. That order revoked a 2000 executive order from President Bill Clinton that required agencies to provide information in other languages for people with limited English skills.

“Agencies should strive to operate solely in English,” the guidance states.

Under the attorney general’s memo, agencies should use English for official business, public communications, forms, applications, websites, outreach materials, internal communications and training, unless another language is required by law or necessary for an agency’s mission.

The policy includes exceptions. Multilingual help will continue where required by the Constitution, federal law, court orders or binding regulations, and in areas such as national security, immigration enforcement, law enforcement, disaster preparedness, public health and safety, health care and court proceedings. Where other languages are needed, agencies are told to use the least burdensome, most cost-effective method. The English version of any document is the official one.

Some agencies have already moved. The Department of Housing and Urban Development dropped non-English languages from its business in August, and the General Services Administration this week ended the Spanish version of USA.gov, which had been available since 2003.

The public can comment on the guidance through Jan. 11, 2027.

The idea is popular with voters. According to Ballotpedia, 13 states have voted on English-only ballot measures, and all but one approved them.

scraped.description: A new UN watchdog report says it cannot verify Iran’s near-weapons-grade uranium and calls the lack of access a proliferation concern.
scraped.h1: Iran Shuts Out Nuclear Inspectors, Blames Trump’s Threats
scraped.body_text:
Iran has told the United Nations nuclear watchdog that inspections of its nuclear program cannot resume while it is under threat from the United States, The Associated Press reported.

The International Atomic Energy Agency revealed Iran’s position in a confidential report circulated to member states Friday. The agency urged Tehran to restore access for its inspectors, saying it is essential to its job of monitoring the country’s nuclear program.

According to the report, the lack of information about Iran’s nuclear sites and material is “a matter of proliferation concern” that “needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency.” The agency said it is “fully prepared to resume its safeguards activities in Iran at short notice.”

Iran has allowed only very limited inspections since the United States and Israel struck its nuclear facilities in June 2025. Since then, the IAEA has been unable to verify the status of Iran’s stockpile of uranium enriched close to weapons grade.

Of particular concern is an underground enrichment facility near Isfahan. Iran declared the plant in 2025 but has never let inspectors in. The agency does not know its precise location or whether it contains nuclear material, though the report did not establish that enrichment is taking place there.

Tehran blamed Washington. Iran told the agency that talks on resuming inspections cannot go forward amid what it called “persistent, explicit, and public threats by the President of the United States of America” to carry out further attacks. It said the issue would not be resolved “until the root causes of the present situation are addressed.”

IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi urged Iran to restore access and to consider limited technical steps that could make inspection visits possible.

scraped.h1: From gay marriage to ‘legally enshrining polyamorous couples’: John Doyle asks Michael Knowles how it led to this
scraped.body_text:
Knowles joins Doyle to argue that activist judges and left-wing political movements — not changing public opinion — drove the dramatic redefinition of marriage in America.

First came same-sex marriage. Now, parts of California are taking another step toward redefining marriage — this time by recognizing polyamorous relationships.

“We have Los Angeles County now legally enshrining polyamorous couples,” BlazeTV host John Doyle begins. “You’ve got throuples, foursomes, not in a golf-concerned context, as basically being the legal equivalent of marriage.”

This concept, he explains, originated “from this idea of having these kinds of deviant relationships be granted equal status to marriage under the law.”

“California struck down gay marriage in 2008 when it was put to a democratic vote," Doyle says, "and then less than 10 years later, the Supreme Court of course discovers the right to marry a man if you are a man in the Constitution.”

“So it seems to be the result less of this kind of slippery slope, more of just like hyperfocused, dedicated leftist activism,” he adds, asking Daily Wire host Michael Knowles, “What do you make of all of this?”

Knowles recalls that Andrew Breitbart, whom he describes as “the king of the Hollywood conservatives” aided in organizing Friends of Abe.

“There are a lot of conservatives in California. It’s just that there were more left-wingers,” he tells Doyle.

“So Breitbart had this line that went very, very viral, which is that ‘politics is downstream of culture.’ And really what he was saying was we need to get involved in the arts and the media and take over all those institutions,” Knowles explains.

Although he admits that Breitbart “was totally right about that,” he also notes that “some people made an idol out of that maxim and tried to raise it to the level of political philosophy."

“It isn’t quite that because what you saw with Prop 8 and now the throuples … in California is the opposite,” he says.

“You see that culture is downstream of politics,” Knowles argues.

“When it was put up for a vote, when the popular culture was asked, do you want gay marriage? The culture said, ‘No, we don’t want that,’ even in liberal California,” he explains.

But Knowles argues that the issue ultimately wasn't left to voters.

Rather, Supreme Court Justice Anthony Kennedy, whom Knowles sarcastically calls “a romantic poet,” invoked “the right to intimacy that we have.”

“And he just rewrote the Constitution to say that two fellas can get married. Not merely rewriting the Constitution, but also trying to rewrite natural law,” he explains.

“And after that, guess what? If you put it up to a vote, people will vote for it. They will support it,” he continues. “Now, that’s declined a little bit in recent years as the reality of these weird sexual relationships has come to light, but nevertheless, it’s still majority support.”

“So you see that in California, and you see it elsewhere in the country,” he adds.

scraped.title: Democrats are not hiding their plans for 2027 | Blaze Media
scraped.description: Incoming Democrats have been honest about one thing — they plan to abuse their power to settle political scores.
scraped.author: https://www.facebook.com/140738092630206
scraped.h1: Democrats are not hiding their plans for 2027
scraped.body_text:
Now that they won, congressional Democrats admit they are out for revenge, writes Rep. Pat Fallon.

Incoming Democrats have been honest about one thing — they plan to abuse their power to settle political scores.

By their own words, they're not here to legislate or conduct genuine oversight. They’re here to issue blanket subpoenas and intimidate folks who are not part of the Democratic Machine from serving in government. In fact, Democrats’ public comments have more in common with practices in Third World banana republics than the America we are familiar with.

'They are going to need to plant new forests for all of the subpoenas we’ll be printing.'

The Supreme Court settled this question decades ago: “Investigations conducted solely for the personal aggrandizement of the investigators or to ‘punish’ those investigated are indefensible.”

In Watkins v. United States , Chief Justice Earl Warren’s majority opinion drew a clear line: “No inquiry is an end in itself; it must be related to, and in furtherance of, a legitimate task of the Congress.” Since 1957, courts have continually ruled that congressional investigations that primarily seek to expose or punish are not a valid legislative function.

Democrats have been explicit about their wish to investigate and prosecute their political opponents in the past. This is distinct from using the investigative process for purely legislative means. After the past decade of lawfare waged by the left, this behavior is nothing new.

Let’s review some of the recent comments by members of the incoming Democrat majority.

Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.): “If you’re involved in any way with the Trumps, and if you’re part of an American business, you’re going to respond to the Congress.”

Garcia treats mere association with the 45th President as sufficient to compel disclosure of private business matters. The case can be made that all 36 million businesses in the country are involved with the executive branch in some capacity. The incoming Oversight Chairman lacks the general authority to expose the private affairs of individuals without justification in terms of the function of Congress.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.): “ There are so many criminals in this administration … Day one, we need to be opening investigations into the heads of every single one of these agencies, and we need to hold them accountable .”

Ocasio-Cortez labels her political targets “criminals” and calls for using the congressional investigative process to hold every agency head accountable. This is punishment, as it does not serve a legislative purpose.

RELATED: The GOP’s old dogs had better learn some new tricks

Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images

Rep. Analilia Mejia (D-N.J.): “ We’re going to toss out subpoenas like Mardi Gras beads .”

Rep. Mejia treats subpoenas as a mass, indiscriminate tool of pressure rather than targeted legislative inquiry. Again, this is using the legislative process as a penalty or sanction against individuals, rather than for a clear legislative purpose.

Sen. Ed Markey (D-Mass.): “ They are going to need to plant new forests for all of the subpoenas we’ll be printing .”

Markey is no stranger to the legislative process, having served 20 terms in the House and three so far in the Senate. His statement celebrates the volume of compulsory process as the point, implying burden (as punishment) as the goal. This practice is not a valid use of legislative investigative powers according to Watkins v. United States .

These direct quotes by congressional Democrats reflect their eagerness to use their elected offices, not for any specific legislative purpose, but to settle scores with their political opponents.

Democrats are open about their wish to harass or intimidate targets rather than gather facts needed for legislation as a means to generate headlines or political damage. Not only would this be unconstitutional, it’s a promise to abuse power, made by the crowd that claims to be “protecting democracy.”

Editor's note: A version of this article appeared originally on X .

Pat Fallon

scraped.author: https://www.facebook.com/140738092630206
scraped.h1: Son of ex-CIA chief John Brennan arrested for allegedly transporting child porn — but the investigation began during the Biden era
scraped.body_text:
Kyle Brennan's residence was searched in 2024, and the FBI cracked his phone two years later, according to the DOJ.

The son of the head of the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency during the Obama administration was arrested after officials say they found horrific child pornography on his device.

Kyle Owen Brennan was arrested on Friday afternoon at his workplace in Herndon, Virginia, according to the Daily Mail.

The FBI claimed in the criminal complaint that on Kyle Brennan's iPhone, agents had 'observed approximately 88 images that appeared to depict minor girls, including prepubescent girls.'

Brennan's father is John Brennan, who has been accused of politicizing the CIA during the Obama administration.

The FBI claimed in the criminal complaint that on Kyle Brennan's iPhone, agents had "observed approximately 88 images that appeared to depict minor girls, including prepubescent girls, engaged in sexually explicit conduct."

One photograph allegedly showed a "fully nude, pubescent minor girl" with her wrists and ankles bound and a gag in her mouth, the complaint said.

A press release from the U.S. Attorney's Office in Virginia said that a tip from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children led to Warrenton police identifying Brennan as the owner of an account allegedly used to upload suspected child pornography.

The complaint indicated that the suspect's phone was obtained when the Fauquier County Sheriff's Office executed a search warrant at his residence in July 2024, when President Joe Biden was still in office. In early October 2026, the case was referred to the FBI, which was able to search the contents of the phone.

Kyle Brennan made his first appearance in court on Friday in the Eastern District of Virginia. Brennan is facing a felony charge of transportation of child pornography and faces a mandatory minimum prison sentence of five years and up to 20 years if convicted.

The federal public defender listed as representing Brennan did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Blaze News.

Both foreign and domestic intelligence services are known to have the ability to upload incriminating files onto devices connected to the internet.

RELATED: Trump says 'irrefutable proof' shows Obama is guilty of 'treason' — and names other Dems in 'biggest scandal' in US history

Kyle's father, John Brennan, has been a vocal critic of President Donald Trump and his administration for over a decade. John Brennan has even been accused of abusing his authority while in office by falsely accusing Trump of colluding with Russia to win the 2016 election.

John Brennan was also one of the 51 former U.S. intelligence officials who signed a public letter identifying the Hunter Biden laptop story that broke just before the 2020 election as having all of the "classic earmarks of a Russian information operation."

items.title: The South deals blow to racist gerrymandering in historic midterm elections. What comes next?
items.summary: Right now, the South is showing working people how to fight back to protect the gains won in struggle.

scraped.title: The South deals blow to racist gerrymandering in historic midterm...
scraped.description: The November 3 midterms thrust the South in the spotlight. Black voter turnout surged across Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas, Georgia, Alabama, Flo
scraped.author: Deja Gaston
scraped.h1: The South deals blow to racist gerrymandering in historic midterm elections. What comes next?
scraped.body_text:
The November 3 midterms thrust the South in the spotlight. Black voter turnout surged across Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas, Georgia, Alabama, Florida, and Louisiana. The historic “flipping” of Texas, South Carolina, and now Mississippi – all of which elected Democratic senators or governors for the first time in decades – would not have been possible without historic Black voter turnout. The results expose the lie in the characterization of Southern states as unsalvageable, “deep red” backwaters. The stereotype of Southerners as “backwards” erases the heroism of the Black freedom struggle and overlooks the centrality of the Black nation as the engine for social change. Tired tropes of Southerners as “racist” and “uneducated” flatten the political dynamism of the multinational Southern working class, erase its militant labor history and ignore the underlying economic pressures that drew many white working class Southerners toward the Trump camp in the first place.

Despite decades of voter suppression, racial gerrymandering and the dismantling of federal voting protections, Southerners, and Black voters in particular, struck back.

The midterm elections saw Black voters mobilize in historic numbers. This spring, the Republican Party led a vicious redistricting campaign to kneecap Black voting power. The landmark Supreme Court decision Louisiana v Callais significantly weakened the Voting Rights Act and wiped Louisiana’s second majority-Black congressional district off the map. Subsequently, Louisiana’s pro-Trump governor, Jeff Landry, undemocratically suspended the primary elections for U.S. House races, pushing the elections from May to July. Following the Supreme Court decision, Republican-led redistricting efforts swept across the South, giving Republicans the green light to redraw congressional maps at the disadvantage of Black voters in Alabama, Georgia, Florida, Mississippi, South Carolina and Tennessee.

The right wing’s attempt to squash the Black vote backfired, contributing to high-profile seat flips in Texas, South Carolina, Alabama and Mississippi. Black voter turnout reached approximately 96% of 2024 presidential year levels, compared with 71% for white and other voters. In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor. In South Carolina, Democrat Annie Andrews defeated Republican Darline Graham in a state Donald Trump had carried by 18 percentage points.

In Alabama, the GOP dominated legislature gerrymandered congressional maps after the Louisiana v. Callais decision. Despite a map that reduced the Black voting age population in one district from about 49% to just under 40%, Representative Shomari Figures retained his seat.

Louisiana shows both the possibilities and limitations of this shift. Democrat Jamie Davis lost his Senate race to Republican Julia Letlow by approximately 25,857 votes. Davis received 720,106 votes, the largest number ever received by a Black candidate in a Louisiana statewide election. Turnout reached approximately 49.3%, and Black voters accounted for 34.4% of early voters. Every parish shifted toward the Democratic candidate compared with 2024. Yet this mobilization was not enough to overcome the Republican advantage statewide.

The ruling class fears Black political participation, even in the controlled parameters of capitalist elections. The Trump administration has been waging an all-out assault on Black America, by rolling back key Civil Rights legislation barring workplace and housing discrimination, gutting social programs, dismantling DEI and firing many Black federal employees

In the Radical Reconstruction era of the 1860s and 70s, Black Southerners achieved far-reaching gains in political representation, only to be smashed by the pro-confederate backlash which enacted the Black Codes in an attempt to re-enslave the Black population. In 1866 in New Orleans, white supremacists carried out a massacre of over a hundred Black freedmen and white Radical Republicans who had convened a meeting to organize against the Black Codes. The violent counterrevolution of white supremacy ushered in the era of Jim Crow, poll taxes, literacy tests and voter intimidation.

During the Civil Rights Revolution, it was Black Southerners who became the protagonists again. People came out daily to the streets to demonstrate, form mass organizations, launch boycotts and form strategic alliances. Landmark legislation like the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 were not handed down as benevolent gestures from the ruling class, they were fought for and won by a militant mass struggle led by Black Southerners. This is why Black America is the detonator for social transformation in the United States.

The question is not whether or not the Black Belt has an appetite to resist a return to the plantation system. It’s about what the most effective tool is to smash the modern counterrevolution. Even when people retain the formal right to vote, the elites who run the capitalist system can always intervene to shape the system on their behalf. While millions of people can participate in elections, politicians and the unelected Supreme Court can manipulate district boundaries through gerrymandering to diminish the political influence of entire communities.

The struggle for voting rights established the right to participate in ruling class elections. But democracy cannot be confined to the ballot box while corporate executives and private owners control working people’s destinies and material conditions. Working class people need real democratic control over society!

The history of Black political struggle in the South offers a foundation for this vision. Formerly enslaved Africans and freedmen led the first general strike in the U.S. and fought in the Civil War overthrowing the slavocracy of the South. Black southerners anchored the struggle against Jim Crow apartheid and mobilized for voting rights. Black America has risen up against police brutality and mass incarceration. For decades, the Black political struggle demonstrated the power of organized collective action.

Right now, the South is showing working people how to fight back to protect the gains won in struggle. But it is not enough to just defend those rights.

Expanding these gains to codified rights, requires fighting against this racist, capitalist system. The struggle for democracy in the South must become the struggle for working class power to complete the gains from the Reconstruction Era and towards a Third Reconstruction.

As legendary New Orleans Black Panther Malik Rahim proclaims, “As goes the South, So goes America. So goes America, so goes the world as we know it!”

The Party for Socialism and Liberation is comprised of leaders and activists, workers and students, of all backgrounds. Organized in branches across the country, our mission is to link the everyday struggles of oppressed and exploited people to the fight for a new world. Interested in joining? Click here!

items.title: “No cuts!”—Protest at Frankfurt’s Goethe University against the devastation of education
items.summary: University management plans to axe 60 professorships, merge faculties and destroy numerous fixed-term posts.

scraped.title: “No cuts!”—Protest at Frankfurt’s Goethe University against the devastation of education
scraped.description: University management plans to axe 60 professorships, merge faculties and destroy numerous fixed-term posts.
scraped.h1: Read more
scraped.body_text:
“No cuts!”—under this slogan, around 300 employees, students, professors, lecturers and research staff gathered on Tuesday, November 3, for an information event in the lecture hall building of Goethe University in Frankfurt’s Westend district. The university’s executive board had issued the invitation under the title “Goethe let’s talk,” but there was great anger and unrest among those present.

Shortly beforehand, the details of the executive board’s new package of cuts had become known. A 59-page paper, initially leaked only to the media, has since also been made available to members of the university on the intranet. According to this document, Goethe University is to be completely restructured within five years. Of the 600 professorships, around 60 are to be axed, the number of faculties halved and several institutes closed. Many staff on fixed-term contracts will lose their jobs in the coming months. As one of them told the Frankfurter Rundschau after the meeting, “The executive board explicitly admitted today that it cannot offer any prospects for employees on fixed-term contracts.”

The devastating cuts are the direct result of the reductions that Hesse’s state Science Minister Timon Gremmels (Social Democrats, SPD) and State Premier Boris Rhein (Christian Democrats, CDU) decided on last year. The “Hesse Higher Education Pact 2026–2031” was signed on July 17, 2025. It covers the state’s 14 public universities and provides for budget cuts of €30 million for 2026 alone.

For the winter semester that has just begun, Goethe University has already reduced the number of study places by 455—almost 10 percent of the roughly 4,600 new students admitted the previous year. Hirings and professorial appointments have been suspended, and severe savings are being made in the staffing, materials and investment budgets.

Yet the Higher Education Pact is not the only reason for the slash-and-burn policy at one of Germany’s largest and most renowned universities. Speaking to the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung ( FAZ ), university President Enrico Schleiff stressed, “We would have initiated the development process arising from the Higher Education Pact even without the pressure to make savings.” His plans go far beyond the demands of the pact. The concept presented internally on October 21 envisages as strategic priorities a concentration on digitalisation and artificial intelligence, as well as a research alliance with the University of Mainz and the Technical University of Darmstadt.

The existing 16 faculties are to be turned into seven, with smaller institutes dissolved and large, comprehensive faculties created. In the humanities alone, at least 18 professorships are to go, and five faculties are to be reduced to two. One of the two is to be called “History, Culture and Religion” and will merge history with philosophy, religious and cultural studies, the theologies and classical studies. The second, under the title “Literature, Language and Art,” is to comprise modern and East Asian philologies, African studies, musicology, art history and art education.

The plans are meeting with broad criticism, which increasingly raises fundamental questions. But the money is obviously there. The Bundeswehr (Armed Forces) and the arms companies are raking in vast sums, and the DAX stock index is climbing to one record high after another, while massive cuts are being made to higher education and education as a whole.

Nine Frankfurt sociology professors, including Stephan Lessenich, director of the Institute for Social Research, have also sharply criticised the cuts. In an open letter, they denounced “the scandalous casualisation of academic and administrative employment, the erosion of core funding in favour of ‘flagship projects,’ the downgrading of students to factors in a business cost-benefit calculation, the forced erosion of the unity of research and teaching, the by now routine undermining of academic self-governance.”

They had remained silent long enough, they wrote, but “In recent months, conditions at German universities, and especially at Goethe University, have come to a head in a way that makes further professorial silence possible only at the quite obvious price of either self-abandonment or the denial of reality.”

They went on to write that Goethe University was on the way to becoming an “academically gutted, downright anti-scholarly ‘lean university,’” guided by “management strategies and governance illusions borrowed from outdated textbooks.” In doing so, the executive board was ignoring the “challenges—from the neo-fascist, systematic subversion of democratic institutions to the further intensified plundering of the foundations of existence.” Finally, the professors committed themselves to fighting for adequate education funding and for the “renegotiation of the Hesse Higher Education Pact, for the unity of research and teaching, and for a democratic and anti-fascist university.”

On October 31, hundreds of Goethe University students took part in the Gen Z protests. One orgy of cuts after another has provoked protests not only at Goethe University but also at many other universities in Hesse and across Germany.

In Kassel, students recently occupied their university to resist the scrapping of the civil clause ( Zivilklausel )—the university’s self-imposed commitment that its research and teaching must serve exclusively civilian purposes. The university responded with a brutal police operation. As the WSWS has reported , the senate of the University of Kassel is seeking to abolish the civil clause in order to enable closer collaboration with the arms industry, with Rheinmetall and KNDS, in a city that is a major centre of arms production.

The protests at the universities are part of the growing youth movement throughout Europe which is directed both against the social devastation and the education emergency and against the extremely dangerous militarisation of society. This movement is international and is developing largely outside the trade unions and establishment parties. Neither Die Linke (Left Party) nor the education union GEW has so far organised any effective action beyond the regional level. In alliance with the capitalist state, they reject any independent movement of workers and young people.

The International Youth and Students for Social Equality (IYSSE), the youth and student organisation of the Sozialistische Gleichheitspartei (Socialist Equality Party, SGP) and the International Committee of the Fourth International, therefore calls on all students who seriously want to fight the devastating cuts at the universities to familiarise themselves with Marxism and the socialist strategy against war and capitalism. The decisive task is to unite the protests and struggles of young people with those of the international working class and to work consciously for the overthrow of the capitalist system.
